name: Determining When at Least One of the Three Boolean Variables is True
description: Construct a program that determines whether at least one of the three boolean variables is true based on the inputs that it receives from the user.

comments.content: We need to read and process the values that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the value of 1st boolean variable.
We need to read the value of the 1st boolean variable and store it in a variable. We read the value of the 1st boolean variable by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean.
Note that if the user provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We prompt the user to enter the value of the 2nd boolean variable.
We need to read the value of the 2nd boolean variable and store it in a variable. We read the value of the 2nd boolean variable by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean.
Note that if the user provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We prompt the user to enter the value of the 3rd boolean variable.
We need to read the value of the 3rd boolean variable and store it in a variable. We read the value of the 3rd boolean variable by calling the nextBoolean() method because this input is a boolean.
Note that if the user provides a non-boolean value, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., boolean.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.
We combine the three conditions sequentially using the || (called or) operator to check if one of the conditions is true.
Note that the || operator yields the result true if at least one of the conditions is true.
This statement prints true/false depending on whether at least one of the three boolean variables is true. The printed value is followed by an end-of-line character in the end.
